messages:
Lina: Quick sync: onboarding pipeline failures again. New quantized models pass the bench but fail in Dedicated due to subtle tokenization/merge quirks. Root cause: bench uses canonical tokenization while runtime uses vendor tokenizer fallback. Need a robust compatibility check. Ideas? cc @Omar @Theo
Omar: We need a lightweight binary-level compat check early in intake. Something like a fingerprint test that verifies tokenization + logits shape on a small canonical corpus. If mismatch, fail fast.
Theo: Agreed. Important that it runs fast and doesn't double-run heavy bench. We can do a "micro-compat" step: 50 canonical prompts, compare tokens+first-token-logits with a tolerance.
Lina: Sketch of micro-compat runner:
```
# run as part of intake
compat_runner --model $BUNDLE --suite canonical-50 --compare tokens,logits --tol 1e-3
```
If tokens differ more than N samples -> reject.
QA-bot: Suggest adding a second check for kv-cache ABI: run a tiny incremental generation sequence and ensure cache hits/lengths are stable. Many regressions show up only when cache is used.
Omar: Good call. Add a two-phase micro-compat: tokenization fingerprint + kv handshake smoke. Both cheap (<1s p/run) if we limit sample size.
Theo: Where do we store tolerances/policy? Could be in model manifest as compat_policy {token_tol: 1e-3, kv_handshake: true}. That allows model owners to escalate if they know binary quirks.
Lina: Hmm manifest additions slow self-serve onboarding. Default policy should be strict, with an intake-appeal path. Only allow override after manual review.
Omar: Implementation detail: bench/admit should record the micro-compat hashes so runtime can detect drift across releases. e.g., store tokenizer_hash and handshake_signature in registry.
Theo: Also add a diagnostic mode that uploads a small payload when compat fails: tokens_before/after diff and a minimal trace (no logits) so engineers can triage without reproing locally. Respect privacy for customer models.
Lina: UX-wise: Console should show a clear "compat fail" message with one-click open issue and pre-filled logs. And a link to a helper tool that reproduces the micro-compat locally.
Omar: Edge case: quantized conversions sometimes change logit scales slightly. Instead of absolute compare, use rank-preservation metric (spearman rho) for top-k logits. That is robust to scaling.
Theo: Nice. So micro-compat rules: tokens identical on >=95% samples; top-5 spearman rho >= 0.98; kv handshake stable. Otherwise fail and route to manual review/canary.
Lina: Action items:
- implement compat_runner prototype (token fingerprint + topk-spearman + kv-handshake)
- add registry fields: tokenizer_hash, compat_signature
- intake: run micro-compat and block/flag accordingly (default block)
- Console: display fail reason + quick repro link
- RFC: policy for manifest overrides & appeal workflow
ingest-bot: Task created: IN-5132 "micro-compat runner + registry fields"
QA-bot: Added test plan template: "compat-smoke-suite" (50 canonical prompts, kv-seq=8, topk=5).
Theo: I'll prototype the runner this week. Will ping when PR is up.
